Cross-domain generalization: a wild-trained USV detector on laboratory mice it never saw

Production detector hard_neg_retrain + soft-notch, applied to lab cohort 131204. Human-verified. 2026-07-05.
Claim. The production CNN was trained exclusively on wild-derived mice (cohort 5970; every training recording dated 2024-09-30 to 2024-10-06, zero lab recordings). Applied with the adaptive soft-notch to laboratory cohort 131204 — a different population and a different recording cage — it detects USVs at 96–100% precision and 97.6–99.7% recall on human review, with its hard rejections correct 30/30. The detector generalizes across the wild→lab domain gap.

1. Result

Two samples of 2-second lab chunks were reviewed by the human annotator (Shachar), each probing a different part of the difficulty distribution. Selection of the second sample was independent of the CNN's output (model-blind random draw, seed 42), which is what makes it an unbiased generalization estimate.

SampleSelectionChunksCNN detectionsFalse pos.Missed USVsPrecisionRecall
High-activity ("hot")picked for most high-confidence events (favourable)6091203100.0%99.7%
Hard-tier randommanual-review + auto-reject, model-blind (unbiased, hardest)601686496.4%97.6%

The hard-tier sample deliberately draws only from the ambiguous (manual-review) and rejected (auto-reject) tiers — the two hardest eighths of the corpus — and excludes the confident majority. It is therefore a lower bound: the full corpus is 73% auto-reject and 19% auto-accept (both near-perfect, below), so corpus-wide accuracy sits above the 96–98% measured on the hard tiers.

2. The rejections are trustworthy (30/30)

The most informative number is one the favourable sample could not produce: of the 30 auto-reject chunks the CNN committed to "nothing here," a human found a missed USV in zero of them. Every false negative in the entire study is a faint extra call inside a chunk where the CNN had already correctly detected 5–10 USVs — never a call in a chunk it rejected outright. A detector's silent drops are where hidden failure usually hides; here the audit of the discard pile came back clean.

3. Both error modes are the hardest possible cases

  • All 6 false positives were a single fire (n_events=1) on an otherwise entirely-noise chunk — and only in the manual-review tier, i.e. exactly where the CNN itself signalled low confidence. Per the annotator, "the noise really is as close as it gets to a USV."
  • All 4 (hard-tier) + 3 (hot) misses were faint, short calls sitting between confidently-detected neighbours — the known hard case for any spectrogram detector.

The errors are not random: the CNN is unsure precisely where a human is unsure. That calibration — on a population it never trained on — is the real signature of generalization, beyond the headline rates.

4. Evidence

5. Method

Detector models/hard_neg_retrain/best_model.pt (production) run via run_batch_detection.py with the full pipeline (temperature T=0.902, hysteresis onset 0.60/sustain 0.40/min-dur 3, FP-filter) plus --soft-notch data/lab_tonal_lines/lab_131204.json (lab tonal line @ 50.7 kHz). Detections read from the cached deterministic run results/batch_lab_full_softnotch_20260513_1538/. Chunks are the 300 kHz resampled lab audio. Hard-tier sample: 30 manual-review + 30 auto-reject drawn model-blind (seed 42), hot chunks excluded. All spectrograms use the canonical STFT grid imported from corpus.py. Galleries: results/lab_hot_notch_gallery/, results/lab_generalization_proof/random_sample_review.html.

6. Honest caveats

  • Ground truth is human visual review by one expert annotator, not an independent label set; the counts are that reviewer's verdict.
  • The "hot" 100%/99.7% is on a CNN-confidence-selected subset and must not be read as the corpus rate; the unbiased number is the hard-tier 96.4%/97.6%.
  • All figures are lab cohort 131204 (partner-swap assay); generalization to other cages/rigs is untested.
  • The soft-notch removes one calibrated tonal line (50.7 kHz); a second ~63 kHz line is present but un-notched and did not appear to cause false positives.

Detector trained on wild mice, validated here on lab mice it never saw. Precision 96–100%, recall 97.6–99.7%, rejections 30/30 correct, errors confined to the genuinely ambiguous. This is evidence of cross-domain generalization, not a claim of perfection.
